summary: After a discouraging loss and a vow never to run again, a man talks it over with his wife and runs again when the chair calls.
realLife: A former Indiana legislator said a loss left him so discouraged that he decided he would never run again. Years later in 1986 the county party chairman called, said he had run a good campaign and asked him to try for county council. He said he had to think about it, went home and talked it over with his wife, and they decided he would run in a smaller district. He, his wife and his son then went door to door.
gates: The candidate lost a race earlier.
A party leader has asked the candidate to file.
The candidate has a spouse in the household.
weights: How deep the sting of the last loss is.
Whether the spouse backs a second try.
How much smaller the new race is.
inGame: Election results, a candidate filing, a marriage and a family member's help canvassing could carry it; the party chair's call needs a recruiting contact from the party record.

turns.what: The spouse says no and the candidate turns the chair down.
turns.pulledBy: A spouse who dreaded the last campaign, a young family.

turns.what: They agree to run only if the race is smaller and the family canvasses together.
turns.writesBack: Filing for the smaller seat; family members as volunteers.

turns.what: He runs again and loses, and the spouse is the one who says to stop.
turns.writesBack: Election loss; candidate's later filings dropped.
